A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRACE research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations, embedding evaluations on 71,021 retinal ganglion-cell boutons, ablations, and artifact/outlier analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original analyses of 10,322 Neuropixels neurons and experiments varying embedding dimension.

M1.justification: The subset-mean positive pairs, InfoNCE objective with Cauchy similarity, MLP architecture, and full-trial-mean inference remain unchanged. Explicit per-neuron, per-epoch subset resampling clarifies implementation; the higher-dimensional experiments introduce evaluation configurations rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds Allen Institute Neuropixels spiking responses from 10,322 neurons across visual brain regions, using flashes and drifting gratings and evaluating anatomical and functional properties. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained synthetic and retinal calcium-imaging datasets. Non-neuroscience applications remain future proposals.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain CEED, TS2Vec, t-SNE, UMAP, and the TRACE+CEED and TRACE+TS2Vec variants. Table S6 extends the existing comparator set to Neuropixels. Added PCA labels in retained figures clarify existing dimensionality reduction rather than introduce different baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include 25-ms spike binning, brain-area labels, biological-variable kNN regression, Neuropixels-specific hyperparameter searches, and 16- and 128-dimensional evaluations. For the retained calcium experiment, the reported Gaussian-mixture setting changes from four clusters in v1 Section 4.2 to 50 components in v2 Section 4.1. Table 1 remains numerically unchanged, so a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Table S4 adds a focused embedding-dimension sensitivity study. The Neuropixels analyses also examine natural-image selectivity and behavioral modulation, neither used to construct embeddings, testing structure beyond the input stimulus responses. Existing noise, trial-count, augmentation, projection, and outlier analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three-seed synthetic means, 95% confidence intervals, and numerical uncertainties. v2 checklist item 7 newly identifies reported variability as standard deviation across multiple runs and states that displayed embeddings are representative. Table S6 explicitly omits uncertainties as insignificant. No increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: New Neuropixels results include TRACE's ARI of 0.04, kNN accuracy of 23.7%, and best average rank of 1.8 in Table S6. Table S4 adds higher-dimensional results, including TRACE kNN accuracies of 75.3% and 75.5% at dimensions 16 and 128. Table S3 adds aggregate ranks. Previously reported Table 1, Tables S1–S2, and training-time values are retained.

T1.justification: The InfoNCE expression is re-indexed without changing its terms. Equation (4) replaces k ≤ r with k ≤ r/2, making explicit the bound already implied by equal-sized, disjoint subsets of r trials. The remaining mathematical definitions are retained, with no new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract's central claims and the four listed contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion now asserts demonstrated usefulness for Neuropixels spike trains and an advantage from preserving spiking statistics, whereas v1 presents spike-train application as future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific limitation: TRACE is inappropriate when between-trial variation, such as adaptation, is scientifically meaningful. It explains why brain-region labels need not form separate clusters, interprets the new biological-property evaluations, and expands discussion of possible applications beyond neuroscience.

D1.justification: v2 adds Neuropixels preprocessing and hyperparameters and clarifies dynamic trial-subset resampling. It replaces the OSF code-access link with named TRACE and TRACE_experiments repositories and discloses that calcium-imaging data release is deferred. Existing architecture, hardware, and calcium-training details are largely retained; external resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Three references on wearable exercise data, basketball activity recognition, and Speech Commands are added to motivate future applications. The core positioning relative to contrastive learning and visualization methods remains unchanged. The Neuropixels dataset publication was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The scientific section sequence and most prose remain intact. Local revisions clarify positive-pair notation and dataset descriptions, while a Neuropixels results subsection, preprocessing subsection, acknowledgments, expanded conclusion, and conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: Two new multipanel Neuropixels figures and two new result tables substantially extend the visual presentation. Figure 4 rearranges artifact panels and removes their OOi, RTi, and depth histograms. Table S3 gains a rank column, and several retained figures and tables receive clearer labels, captions, and highlighting.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves spike-train validation to future work; v2 supplies a substantial evaluation across 10,322 Neuropixels neurons, biological-property analyses beyond the embedding inputs, and dimension-sensitivity tests. This materially strengthens evidence beyond the original calcium-imaging case and clarifies an important applicability limit. These gains outweigh remaining reporting ambiguities: the unexplained four-to-50 clustering change accompanies unchanged Table 1 values, and Table S6's correlation-versus-regression assignments conflict with the main text.
